prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production transparent sprite animation sheet for a hand-painted top-down survival game.
Input image 1 is a STYLE and WATER MOTION reference only. Do not copy its rocks or ground.
Create exactly TWELVE chronological animation frames in a precise 4-column by 3-row grid, equal cells, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Full canvas square, no margins between cells; each cell has generous transparent margins around its effect. This is a looping WHITEWATER EFFECT OVERLAY, not a new waterfall scene.
Within every cell, keep the same fixed silhouette and anchor: a soft broken curtain of thin pale blue-white falling-water ribbons in the upper middle, fanning into lacy churning white foam and small splashes in the lower middle. Near top-down/slightly oblique viewpoint matching the reference's waterfall. Individual translucent strands travel visibly downwards between frames; fine landing spray and tiny foam curls shift outward and dissipate. Twelve closely spaced moments of a steady continuous waterfall, last returns smoothly to first, no growth/shrinking of entire object, no camera movement, no change in width or placement.
Hand-painted highly detailed whitewater like the reference, cool blue shaded translucent water, airy fragmented white highlights; delicate detail rather than a solid white block. Dark and open gaps must be TRANSPARENT, and the existing blue river will show through them.
No rocks, no ground, no riverbanks, no blue rectangular background, no plants, no text, no numbering, no border, no grid lines, no labels, no dramatic mist cloud. Only the animated translucent whitewater and landing foam on a genuinely transparent background.
